GRIEVANCE XXV ◆ LIBERTY AND DUE PROCESS

He has defended federal officers after citizens were killed, even as evidence and the demands of local justice called official accounts into question.

THE RECORD SHOWS

Federal immigration officers fatally shot U.S. citizens Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis; investigations and litigation have disputed the officers’ conduct and initial official narratives.

Both deaths occurred during the administration’s intensive immigration enforcement operations in January 2026. Video and witness evidence challenged aspects of early federal descriptions. State investigators said federal authorities initially withheld materials, before turning over evidence in July. Good’s family sued in October; the White House called the suits baseless. This page does not prejudge individual criminal liability.

A DOCUMENTED SEQUENCE

3 MILESTONES
  1. January 2026Immigration agents fatally shot Renee Good and Alex Pretti during separate enforcement encounters in Minneapolis.
  2. July 2026After disputes over access, federal officials provided investigative materials to Minnesota authorities.
  3. October 2026Good’s surviving relatives filed civil claims; the White House denied wrongdoing.

WHAT THE RECORD DOES NOT ESTABLISH

The deaths, investigations, and lawsuits are documented. Pending allegations of excessive force or cover-up are not presented as final criminal judgments.
